text:
maria: FYI - customer (tenant: acme-io) reporting repeated 504s on streaming completions since ~08:12 UTC. They get partial chunks then a 504. Happening across eu1/us1. sample trace: trace=abc123

maria: quick curl they used:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-std","input":"<very large prompt>"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream | sed -n '1,120p'
```

sam: I see p95 write latency spike on frontdoor at same time. frontdoor metrics show many connections in WRITE_WAIT for >8s — looks like socket send buffer filling then stall. suspect proxy buffer bloat + upstream backpressure when backend stalls emitting tokens.

maria: snippets from edge logs around trace abc123:
```
[08:12:42] edge: conn_id=5454 stream_id=abc123 upstream_write: wrote 0 bytes, errno=EAGAIN after 10000ms
[08:12:52] edge: conn_id=5454 stream_id=abc123 downstream_close: client read timeout -> 504
```

devon: do we have a recent config change? runtime batching windows changed yesterday? which pool (gpu-pool-7)?

maria: customer said nothing changed on their side. usage pattern is large streaming model responses (embeds+chat). I can repro locally with a large prompt + streaming chunk size >1MB.

ryan: please run quick checks on the affected nodes: `ss -tnp | grep :443` to see socket states, and `netstat -s | grep -i retrans` for retransmits. Also check `envoy` upstream flush settings — if envoy is buffering large chunks we can hit kernel send buffer limits.

sam: I grabbed a short time window pcap and saw long gaps where kernel send queue was full (snd_queuelen grew). Also noticed envoy config has `proxy_buffering: on` in a migrated nginx template for streaming endpoints — that combination can cause large in-memory buffers then slow unwinding under backpressure.

maria: repro steps I used (local):
1) POST to /v1/stream with a prompt that triggers 1.5MB of initial tokens
2) client reads stream slowly (~50kb/s) to simulate mobile client
3) edge logs show upstream_write EAGAIN then 504

maria: sample python repro (short):
```python
import requests
resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, stream=True)
for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=32768):
    time.sleep(0.05)  # slow reader
    print(chunk)
```

ops-bot: Incident INC-4893 created and linked to trace abc123. Pager duty alerted on p95 gateway errors :eyes:

sam: short-term mitigations:
- disable nginx proxy_buffering for streaming routes (set `proxy_buffering off`)
- reduce large chunking (limit server chunk sizes)
- temporarily increase kernel `net.core.wmem_max` and `net.ipv4.tcp_wmem` on affected frontdoors
- lower runtime batch emission window so model emits smaller chunks more frequently

ryan: long-term: add backpressure-aware streaming in runtime (smaller atomic writes, monitor sndq depth) and add edge metric for `socket_sndq_bytes` per conn. Also add automatic fallback to smaller chunk sizes when client RTT or slow-read is detected.

devon: I can roll nginx change to turn off proxy_buffering on canary frontdoors within 10m. Who wants to own kernel param change?

sam: I'll take kernel tweak for the hotfix (increase wmem and restart edge workers one at a time). I'll also roll the runtime batch window reduction as a config flag to reduce emission size.

maria: customer impacted heavily — I've escalated to CSM and let them know we're deploying mitigations. Please post progress here. :thumbsup:

sam: hotfix rollout started to canary eu1 at 08:40 UTC: nginx proxy_buffering off, monitor p95 write latency.

ryan: capturing tcpdump on canary node now and streaming to the incident ticket (pcap link added).

maria: thanks team. if mitigations work we'll schedule a postmortem and a runbook for streaming chunk/backpressure incidents.

sam: update 08:52 UTC — canary p95 write latency down 60%, no new 504s in window. continuing rollout. :white_check_mark:
